verdict.rationale: BugSnag's docs say events are grouped by error class plus the file and line of the top in-project stack frame, and that the reason for each grouping is shown in the error view. The same page says a range of custom options lets you tailor grouping per project. Missing for 10: detail on what the custom grouping options are (e.g. custom fingerprints or merge/unmerge), evidence of handling volume at the scale of thousands of events, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the platform groups thousands of duplicate events into one issue via stack-trace fingerprinting, and I can customize the grouping when it gets it wrong

citations.quote: Grouped with other events sharing the same error class, file and line number of the top in-project stack frame of the innermost exception.
Individual events are grouped into errors in your inbox and the reason for the grouping is shown at the top of the error view
if you would like to tailor the grouping behavior to your project, a range of custom options are available
